chunks: Hammad narrated from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever arrives after the Tarwiah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah) by ten days, it is obligatory upon him to perform complete prayer (four rak'ahs) while he is in the status of Ahl al-Makkah (residents of Mecca). When he goes out to Mina, it becomes obligatory upon him to shorten prayer (two rak'ahs). When he visits the House (Kaaba), he completes his prayer. And upon him is complete prayer when he returns to Mina until he departs."

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, day of Tarwiah

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shortening or completing prayer during Hajj based on arrival time and location?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the *Muqim* (resident) and *Musafir* (traveler) statuses during Hajj, specifically addressing those who arrive after the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah (Yaw al-Tarwiyah). It establishes that such pilgrims are treated as residents of Mecca until they depart for Mina, at which point they shorten their prayers, and must resume full prayers upon returning to Mina for the stay until the final departure (Nafar). This ruling highlights the dynamic nature of prayer length based on the pilgrim's changing geographical and legal status within the sacred precincts.
